subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Which of the three requested tracks should OpenClaw core own now, and which should stay in plugin/context-engine design until a missing core seam is proven?
rationale: The issue adds durable tool schemas, context/session storage semantics, config knobs, and runner enforcement behavior; automation cannot choose those ownership and compatibility boundaries safely.

options.title: Split And Sponsor Missing Core Seams
options.body: Keep this umbrella open while maintainers separately decide batching, context lifecycle, and plan-gating contracts, adding core APIs only where existing plugin/context-engine hooks cannot support the workflow.

options.title: Route Through Plugins First
options.body: Document and encourage plugin/context-engine approaches until a narrower issue proves a concrete missing core API.

options.title: Defer Native Orchestration
options.body: Decline the umbrella direction for now as too broad for core while leaving narrower regressions or missing APIs to separate issues.

recommendation.title: Split And Sponsor Missing Core Seams
recommendation.body: Keep this umbrella open while maintainers separately decide batching, context lifecycle, and plan-gating contracts, adding core APIs only where existing plugin/context-engine hooks cannot support the workflow.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest prior-review and adjacent-history signal across update_plan, strict-agentic execution, file-tool parameters, and runner behavior.
